Amr ibn al-As.fact: He set up Fustat as the provincial capital with the mosque later called after him at its center. Amr ruled relatively independently, acquired significant wealth, and upheld the interests of the Arab conquerors who formed Fustat's garrison in relation to the central authorities in Medina.

Amr ibn al-As.subject: Defence & Security
Amr ibn al-As.question: After gradually diluting Amr's authority, _____ (r
Amr ibn al-As.fact: After gradually diluting Amr's authority, Caliph Uthman (r.

Amr ibn al-As.subject: Defence & Security
Amr ibn al-As.question: 644–656) dismissed him in 646 after accusations of incompetence from his successor _____ ibn Sa'd
Amr ibn al-As.fact: 644–656) dismissed him in 646 after accusations of incompetence from his successor Abd Allah ibn Sa'd.

Amr ibn al-As.subject: Defence & Security
Amr ibn al-As.question: After mutineers from Egypt assassinated _____, Amr distanced himself from their cause, despite previously instigating opposition against Uthman
Amr ibn al-As.fact: After gradually diluting Amr's authority, Caliph Uthman (r. After mutineers from Egypt assassinated Uthman, Amr distanced himself from their cause, despite previously instigating opposition against Uthman.

Amr ibn al-As.subject: Defence & Security
Amr ibn al-As.question: In the ensuing _____, Amr joined Mu'awiya ibn Abi Sufyan against Caliph Ali (r
Amr ibn al-As.fact: In the ensuing First Fitna, Amr joined Mu'awiya ibn Abi Sufyan against Caliph Ali (r.

Amr ibn al-As.subject: Defence & Security
Amr ibn al-As.question: 656–661) due to promises of the governorship of _____ and its tax revenues
Amr ibn al-As.fact: After mutineers from Egypt assassinated Uthman, Amr distanced himself from their cause, despite previously instigating opposition against Uthman. 656–661) due to promises of the governorship of Egypt and its tax revenues.

Amr ibn al-As.subject: Defence & Security
Amr ibn al-As.question: Afterward, he wrested control of Egypt from Ali's loyalists, killing its governor Muhammad ibn _____, and assumed the governorship instead
Amr ibn al-As.fact: Afterward, he wrested control of Egypt from Ali's loyalists, killing its governor Muhammad ibn Abi Bakr, and assumed the governorship instead.

Amr ibn al-As.subject: Defence & Security
Amr ibn al-As.question: Mu'awiya kept him in his post after establishing the _____ in 661 and Amr ruled the province until his death
Amr ibn al-As.fact: Mu'awiya kept him in his post after establishing the Umayyad Caliphate in 661 and Amr ruled the province until his death.

Amr ibn al-As.subject: Defence & Security
Amr ibn al-As.question: His father, al-As ibn Wa'il, was a wealthy landowner from the _____ clan of the Quraysh tribe of Mecca
Amr ibn al-As.fact: His father, al-As ibn Wa'il, was a wealthy landowner from the Banu Sahm clan of the Quraysh tribe of Mecca.

Amr ibn al-As.subject: Defence & Security
Amr ibn al-As.question: 622, Amr inherited from him the lucrative al-_____ estate and vineyards near Ta'if
Amr ibn al-As.fact: 622, Amr inherited from him the lucrative al-Waht estate and vineyards near Ta'if.

Amr ibn al-As.subject: Defence & Security
Amr ibn al-As.question: Amr's mother was al-_____ bint Harmala from the Banu Jallan clan of the Anaza tribe
Amr ibn al-As.fact: Amr's mother was al-Nabigha bint Harmala from the Banu Jallan clan of the Anaza tribe.

Amr ibn al-As.subject: Defence & Security
Amr ibn al-As.question: She had been taken captive and sold, in succession, to several members of the _____, one of whom was Amr's father
Amr ibn al-As.fact: She had been taken captive and sold, in succession, to several members of the Quraysh, one of whom was Amr's father.

Amr ibn al-As.subject: Defence & Security
Amr ibn al-As.question: As such, Amr had two maternal half-brothers, Amr ibn Atatha of the _____ and Uqba ibn Nafi of the Banu Fihr, and a half-sister from the Banu Abd Shams
Amr ibn al-As.fact: As such, Amr had two maternal half-brothers, Amr ibn Atatha of the Banu Adi and Uqba ibn Nafi of the Banu Fihr, and a half-sister from the Banu Abd Shams.

Amr ibn al-As.subject: Defence & Security
Amr ibn al-As.question: There are conflicting reports about when Amr embraced Islam, with the most credible version placing it in 629/630, not long before the conquest of Mecca by _____
Amr ibn al-As.fact: There are conflicting reports about when Amr embraced Islam, with the most credible version placing it in 629/630, not long before the conquest of Mecca by Muhammad. According to Amr's own testimony, transmitted by his fourth-generation descendant Amr ibn Shu'ayb, he converted in Axum in the presence of King Armah (Najashi) and met Muhammad in Medina upon the latter's return from the Battle of Khaybar in 628.

Amr ibn al-As.subject: Defence & Security
Amr ibn al-As.question: According to this account, he converted alongside the _____ ibn al-Walid and Uthman ibn Talha
Amr ibn al-As.fact: According to this account, he converted alongside the Qurayshites Khalid ibn al-Walid and Uthman ibn Talha.

Amr ibn al-As.subject: Defence & Security
Amr ibn al-As.question: Amr conditioned his conversion on the forgiveness of his past sins and an "active part in affairs", according to a report cited by the historian _____ (d
Amr ibn al-As.fact: Amr conditioned his conversion on the forgiveness of his past sins and an "active part in affairs", according to a report cited by the historian Ibn Asakir (d.

Amr ibn al-As.subject: Defence & Security
Amr ibn al-As.question: The purpose of the raid is unclear, though the modern historian _____ speculates that it was to "break up a gathering of hostile tribal groups" possibly backed by the Byzantine Empire
Amr ibn al-As.fact: The purpose of the raid is unclear, though the modern historian Fred Donner speculates that it was to "break up a gathering of hostile tribal groups" possibly backed by the Byzantine Empire.

Amr ibn al-As.subject: Defence & Security
Amr ibn al-As.question: 833) holds that Amr rallied the nomadic Arabs in the region "to make war on [_____] Syria"
Amr ibn al-As.fact: The purpose of the raid is unclear, though the modern historian Fred Donner speculates that it was to "break up a gathering of hostile tribal groups" possibly backed by the Byzantine Empire. 833) holds that Amr rallied the nomadic Arabs in the region "to make war on [Byzantine] Syria".

Amr ibn al-As.subject: Defence & Security
Amr ibn al-As.question: The tribal groups targeted in the raid included the _____'a in general and the Bali specifically
Amr ibn al-As.fact: The tribal groups targeted in the raid included the Quda'a in general and the Bali specifically. Amr's paternal grandmother hailed from the Bali, and this may have motivated his appointment to the command by Muhammad as Amr was instructed to recruit tribesmen from the Bali and the other Quda'a tribes of Balqayn and Banu Udhra.

Amr ibn al-As.subject: Defence & Security
Amr ibn al-As.question: Following the raid, a delegation of the _____ embraced Islam
Amr ibn al-As.fact: The tribal groups targeted in the raid included the Quda'a in general and the Bali specifically. Amr's paternal grandmother hailed from the Bali, and this may have motivated his appointment to the command by Muhammad as Amr was instructed to recruit tribesmen from the Bali and the other Quda'a tribes of Balqayn and Banu Udhra.

Amr ibn al-As.subject: Defence & Security
Amr ibn al-As.question: Amr further consecrated ties with the tribe by marrying a Bali woman, with whom he had his son _____
Amr ibn al-As.fact: Amr's paternal grandmother hailed from the Bali, and this may have motivated his appointment to the command by Muhammad as Amr was instructed to recruit tribesmen from the Bali and the other Quda'a tribes of Balqayn and Banu Udhra. Amr further consecrated ties with the tribe by marrying a Bali woman, with whom he had his son Muhammad.

Amr ibn al-As.subject: Defence & Security
Amr ibn al-As.question: Muhammad appointed Amr as the governor of _____ and he remained there until being informed of Muhammad's death in 632
Amr ibn al-As.fact: Amr further consecrated ties with the tribe by marrying a Bali woman, with whom he had his son Muhammad. Muhammad appointed Amr as the governor of Oman and he remained there until being informed of Muhammad's death in 632.

Amr ibn al-As.subject: Defence & Security
Amr ibn al-As.question: Amr was personally chosen by _____ to deliver a letter calling the kings of Oman, the Julanda brothers Abd and Jayfa, to convert to Islam while being accompanied by Sa'id ibn Aws al-Ansari
Amr ibn al-As.fact: Amr further consecrated ties with the tribe by marrying a Bali woman, with whom he had his son Muhammad. Muhammad appointed Amr as the governor of Oman and he remained there until being informed of Muhammad's death in 632.

Amr ibn al-As.subject: Defence & Security
Amr ibn al-As.question: Propagate Islam and teach the Qur'an and the institutions of the _____." The death of Muhammad prompted several Arab tribes to defect from the nascent Medina-based Muslim polity in the Ridda wars
Amr ibn al-As.fact: Historian Al-Baladhuri reports that on their departure to Sohar, Muhammad said to them: "If these people (of Oman) accept the witness of truth and pledge obedience to Allah and his Prophet, Amr will be the commander, and Abu Zayd will officiate in prayer. Propagate Islam and teach the Qur'an and the institutions of the Prophet." The death of Muhammad prompted several Arab tribes to defect from the nascent Medina-based Muslim polity in the Ridda wars.

Amr ibn al-As.subject: Defence & Security
Amr ibn al-As.question: Muhammad's successor _____ (r
Amr ibn al-As.fact: Muhammad's successor Caliph Abu Bakr (r.

Amr ibn al-As.subject: Defence & Security
Amr ibn al-As.question: 632–634) appointed Amr to rein in the apostate Quda'a tribes, and among those targeted were the _____ branches of the Bali
Amr ibn al-As.fact: 632–634) appointed Amr to rein in the apostate Quda'a tribes, and among those targeted were the Hejazi branches of the Bali.

Amr ibn al-As.subject: Defence & Security
Amr ibn al-As.question: Amr's campaigns, which were supported by the commander _____ ibn Hasana, succeeded in restoring Medina's authority as far as the northern frontier with Syria
Amr ibn al-As.fact: Amr's campaigns, which were supported by the commander Shurahbil ibn Hasana, succeeded in restoring Medina's authority as far as the northern frontier with Syria.

Amr ibn al-As.subject: Defence & Security
Amr ibn al-As.question: The focus of Amr's campaign was _____, to which he had been appointed governor by Abu Bakr before his departure
Amr ibn al-As.fact: The focus of Amr's campaign was Palestine, to which he had been appointed governor by Abu Bakr before his departure.

Amr ibn al-As.subject: Defence & Security
Amr ibn al-As.question: As a _____ merchant Amr was likely already well-acquainted with the routes to Gaza, a principle terminal for Meccan caravans
Amr ibn al-As.fact: As a Qurayshite merchant Amr was likely already well-acquainted with the routes to Gaza, a principle terminal for Meccan caravans.

Amr ibn al-As.subject: Defence & Security
Amr ibn al-As.question: He took the coastal route of the Hejaz, reaching Ayla, a _____ possession since 630, before breaking west into the Negev desert or possibly the Sinai
Amr ibn al-As.fact: He took the coastal route of the Hejaz, reaching Ayla, a Muslim possession since 630, before breaking west into the Negev desert or possibly the Sinai. Most accounts hold that Amr's army was 3,000-strong; the Muhajirun (emigrants from Mecca to Medina) and the Ansar (natives of Medina), who together formed the core of the earliest Muslim converts, dominated his forces according to al-Waqidi (d.

Amr ibn al-As.subject: Defence & Security
Amr ibn al-As.question: He arrived near the villages of _____ and Badan in Gaza's environs where he entered into talks with Gaza's Byzantine commander
Amr ibn al-As.fact: He arrived near the villages of Dathin and Badan in Gaza's environs where he entered into talks with Gaza's Byzantine commander. After the negotiations broke down, Amr's men bested the Byzantines at the Battle of Dathin on 4 February 634 and set up headquarters at Ghamr al-Arabat in the middle of the Wadi Araba.

Amr ibn al-As.subject: Defence & Security
Amr ibn al-As.question: After the negotiations broke down, Amr's men bested the _____ at the Battle of Dathin on 4 February 634 and set up headquarters at Ghamr al-Arabat in the middle of the Wadi Araba
Amr ibn al-As.fact: After the negotiations broke down, Amr's men bested the Byzantines at the Battle of Dathin on 4 February 634 and set up headquarters at Ghamr al-Arabat in the middle of the Wadi Araba.

Amr ibn al-As.subject: Defence & Security
Amr ibn al-As.question: 823), while the 9th-century historian Ibn A'tham holds that Amr's army consisted of 3,300 _____ and allied horsemen, 1,700 horsemen from the Banu Sulaym and 200 from the Yemenite tribe of Madh'hij
Amr ibn al-As.fact: 823), while the 9th-century historian Ibn A'tham holds that Amr's army consisted of 3,300 Qurayshite and allied horsemen, 1,700 horsemen from the Banu Sulaym and 200 from the Yemenite tribe of Madh'hij.

Amr ibn al-As.subject: Defence & Security
Amr ibn al-As.question: Amr conquered the area around Gaza by _____ or March 634 and proceeded to besiege Caesarea, the capital of Byzantine Palestine, in July
Amr ibn al-As.fact: Amr conquered the area around Gaza by February or March 634 and proceeded to besiege Caesarea, the capital of Byzantine Palestine, in July.

Amr ibn al-As.subject: Defence & Security
Amr ibn al-As.question: He soon after abandoned the siege upon the approach of a large _____ army
Amr ibn al-As.fact: Amr conquered the area around Gaza by February or March 634 and proceeded to besiege Caesarea, the capital of Byzantine Palestine, in July. He soon after abandoned the siege upon the approach of a large Byzantine army.

Amr ibn al-As.subject: Defence & Security
Amr ibn al-As.question: Amr occupied numerous towns in Palestine, including _____, Yibna, Amwas, Lydda, Jaffa, Nablus and Sebastia
Amr ibn al-As.fact: Amr occupied numerous towns in Palestine, including Bayt Jibrin, Yibna, Amwas, Lydda, Jaffa, Nablus and Sebastia.

Amr ibn al-As.subject: Defence & Security
Amr ibn al-As.question: Most of these localities surrendered after little resistance due to the flight of _____ troops; consequently, there is scant information about them in the traditional accounts of the conquest
Amr ibn al-As.fact: He soon after abandoned the siege upon the approach of a large Byzantine army. After being reinforced by the remainder of the Muslim armies in Syria, including the new arrivals commanded by Khalid ibn al-Walid, Amr, with overall command of the 20,000-strong Muslim forces, routed the Byzantine army at the Battle of Ajnadayn, the first major confrontation between the Muslims and Byzantium, in July–August 634.

Amr ibn al-As.subject: Defence & Security
Amr ibn al-As.question: 634–644) appointed or confirmed Amr as the commander and governor of the military district of _____
Amr ibn al-As.fact: Amr occupied numerous towns in Palestine, including Bayt Jibrin, Yibna, Amwas, Lydda, Jaffa, Nablus and Sebastia. 634–644) appointed or confirmed Amr as the commander and governor of the military district of Palestine.

Amr ibn al-As.subject: Defence & Security
Amr ibn al-As.question: The Muslims pursued the _____ army northward and besieged them at Pella for four months
Amr ibn al-As.fact: Most of these localities surrendered after little resistance due to the flight of Byzantine troops; consequently, there is scant information about them in the traditional accounts of the conquest. The Muslims pursued the Byzantine army northward and besieged them at Pella for four months.

Amr ibn al-As.subject: Defence & Security
Amr ibn al-As.question: Amr may have retained overall command of the _____ armies until this point, though other accounts assign command to Khalid or Abu Ubayda ibn al-Jarrah
Amr ibn al-As.fact: The Muslims pursued the Byzantine army northward and besieged them at Pella for four months. Amr may have retained overall command of the Muslim armies until this point, though other accounts assign command to Khalid or Abu Ubayda ibn al-Jarrah.

Amr ibn al-As.subject: Defence & Security
Amr ibn al-As.question: In any case, the _____ landed a heavy blow against the Byzantines in the ensuing Battle of Fahl in December 634 or January 635
Amr ibn al-As.fact: The Muslims pursued the Byzantine army northward and besieged them at Pella for four months. In any case, the Muslims landed a heavy blow against the Byzantines in the ensuing Battle of Fahl in December 634 or January 635.

Amr ibn al-As.subject: Defence & Security
Amr ibn al-As.question: Afterward, Amr and _____ may have been sent to besiege Beisan, which capitulated after minor resistance
Amr ibn al-As.fact: Afterward, Amr and Shurahbil may have been sent to besiege Beisan, which capitulated after minor resistance.

Amr ibn al-As.subject: Defence & Security
Amr ibn al-As.question: The Muslims proceeded to besiege _____, where the remnants of the Byzantine army from the battles of Ajnadayn and Fahl had gathered
Amr ibn al-As.fact: The Muslims proceeded to besiege Damascus, where the remnants of the Byzantine army from the battles of Ajnadayn and Fahl had gathered. By August–September 635, Damascus surrendered to the Muslims.

Amr ibn al-As.subject: Defence & Security
Amr ibn al-As.question: Amr was positioned at the _____ gate, the Muslim commanders having each been assigned to block one of the city's entrances
Amr ibn al-As.fact: Amr was positioned at the Bab Tuma gate, the Muslim commanders having each been assigned to block one of the city's entrances.

Amr ibn al-As.subject: Defence & Security
Amr ibn al-As.question: In response to the series of defeats, the _____ emperor Heraclius (r
Amr ibn al-As.fact: In response to the series of defeats, the Byzantine emperor Heraclius (r. 610–641) led a large army in person to confront the Muslims; its rout at the Battle of Yarmouk, in which Amr played a key role by confining the Byzantines between the banks of the Yarmouk River and the Yarmouk's ravine, in August–September 636, paved the way for the rest of Syria's conquest by the Muslims.

Amr ibn al-As.subject: Defence & Security
Amr ibn al-As.question: Following Yarmouk, the _____ attempted to capture Jerusalem, where Amr had previously sent an advance force
Amr ibn al-As.fact: 610–641) led a large army in person to confront the Muslims; its rout at the Battle of Yarmouk, in which Amr played a key role by confining the Byzantines between the banks of the Yarmouk River and the Yarmouk's ravine, in August–September 636, paved the way for the rest of Syria's conquest by the Muslims. Following Yarmouk, the Muslims attempted to capture Jerusalem, where Amr had previously sent an advance force.

Amr ibn al-As.subject: Defence & Security
Amr ibn al-As.question: Abu Ubayda led the siege of _____, in which Amr participated, but the city only surrendered after Caliph Umar arrived in person to conclude a treaty with its defenders
Amr ibn al-As.fact: Following Yarmouk, the Muslims attempted to capture Jerusalem, where Amr had previously sent an advance force. Abu Ubayda led the siege of Jerusalem, in which Amr participated, but the city only surrendered after Caliph Umar arrived in person to conclude a treaty with its defenders.

Amr ibn al-As.subject: Defence & Security
Amr ibn al-As.question: Amr was one of the witnesses of the _____ of Umar
Amr ibn al-As.fact: Abu Ubayda led the siege of Jerusalem, in which Amr participated, but the city only surrendered after Caliph Umar arrived in person to conclude a treaty with its defenders. Amr was one of the witnesses of the Treaty of Umar.

Amr ibn al-As.subject: Defence & Security
Amr ibn al-As.question: From Jerusalem, Amr then proceeded to besiege and capture the city of _____
Amr ibn al-As.fact: From Jerusalem, Amr then proceeded to besiege and capture the city of Gaza.

Amr ibn al-As.subject: Defence & Security
Amr ibn al-As.question: He had established trading interests there before his conversion to _____, making him aware of its importance in international trade
Amr ibn al-As.fact: He had set up trading interests there before his conversion to Islam, making him aware of its importance in international trade.

Amr ibn al-As.subject: Defence & Security
Amr ibn al-As.question: At the head of 4,000 cavalries and with no siege engines, Amr arrived at the frontier town of al-Arish along the northern Sinai coastline on 12 _____ 639
Amr ibn al-As.fact: At the head of 4,000 cavalries and with no siege engines, Amr arrived at the frontier town of al-Arish along the northern Sinai coastline on 12 December 639.

Amr ibn al-As.subject: Defence & Security
Amr ibn al-As.question: He captured the strategic _____ port city of Pelusium (al-Farama) following a month-long siege and moved against Bilbeis, which also fell after a month-long siege
Amr ibn al-As.fact: He captured the strategic Mediterranean port city of Pelusium (al-Farama) following a month-long siege and moved against Bilbeis, which also fell after a month-long siege.

Amr ibn al-As.subject: Defence & Security
Amr ibn al-As.question: Amr halted his campaign before the fortified _____ stronghold of Babylon, at the head of the Nile Delta, and requested reinforcements from Umar
Amr ibn al-As.fact: Amr halted his campaign before the fortified Byzantine stronghold of Babylon, at the head of the Nile Delta, and requested reinforcements from Umar. In the following month, his army decisively defeated the Byzantines at the Battle of Heliopolis.

Amr ibn al-As.subject: Defence & Security
Amr ibn al-As.question: The latter dispatched _____ ibn al-Awwam, a leading Qurayshite companion of Muhammad, with a 4,000-strong force, which joined Amr's camp in June 640
Amr ibn al-As.fact: The latter dispatched Zubayr ibn al-Awwam, a leading Qurayshite companion of Muhammad, with a 4,000-strong force, which joined Amr's camp in June 640.

Amr ibn al-As.subject: Defence & Security
Amr ibn al-As.question: Amr retained the supreme command of _____ forces in Egypt
Amr ibn al-As.fact: Amr retained the supreme command of Arab forces in Egypt.

Amr ibn al-As.subject: Defence & Security
Amr ibn al-As.question: In the following month, his army decisively defeated the _____ at the Battle of Heliopolis
Amr ibn al-As.fact: In the following month, his army decisively defeated the Byzantines at the Battle of Heliopolis.

Amr ibn al-As.subject: Defence & Security
Amr ibn al-As.question: He captured _____ soon after and besieged Babylon
Amr ibn al-As.fact: He captured Memphis soon after and besieged Babylon.

Amr ibn al-As.subject: Defence & Security
Amr ibn al-As.question: During the siege, Amr entered truce negotiations with the _____-based Byzantine governor Cyrus; Emperor Heraclius opposed the talks and recalled Cyrus to Constantinople
Amr ibn al-As.fact: During the siege, Amr entered truce negotiations with the Alexandria-based Byzantine governor Cyrus; Emperor Heraclius opposed the talks and recalled Cyrus to Constantinople. Amr made an agreement with the Byzantine garrison, allowing their peaceful withdrawal toward the provincial capital Alexandria on 9 April 641.

Amr ibn al-As.subject: Defence & Security
Amr ibn al-As.question: Amr made an agreement with the _____ garrison, allowing their peaceful withdrawal toward the provincial capital Alexandria on 9 April 641
Amr ibn al-As.fact: During the siege, Amr entered truce negotiations with the Alexandria-based Byzantine governor Cyrus; Emperor Heraclius opposed the talks and recalled Cyrus to Constantinople. Amr made an agreement with the Byzantine garrison, allowing their peaceful withdrawal toward the provincial capital Alexandria on 9 April 641.

Amr ibn al-As.subject: Defence & Security
Amr ibn al-As.question: Though strong resistance was put up by _____'s defenders, their morale was sapped after news of Heraclius' death in February 641
Amr ibn al-As.fact: He captured Memphis soon after and besieged Babylon. Though strong resistance was put up by Babylon's defenders, their morale was sapped after news of Heraclius' death in February 641.

Amr ibn al-As.subject: Defence & Security
Amr ibn al-As.question: One of them, _____ ibn Hudhafa, captured the Fayyum oasis, Oxyrhynchus (Bahnasa), Hermopolis (el-Ashmunein) and Akhmim, all in Middle Egypt, and an unspecified number of villages in Upper Egypt
Amr ibn al-As.fact: One of them, Kharija ibn Hudhafa, captured the Fayyum oasis, Oxyrhynchus (Bahnasa), Hermopolis (el-Ashmunein) and Akhmim, all in Middle Egypt, and an unspecified number of villages in Upper Egypt.

Amr ibn al-As.subject: Defence & Security
Amr ibn al-As.question: In late 641, Amr besieged _____
Amr ibn al-As.fact: Amr made an agreement with the Byzantine garrison, allowing their peaceful withdrawal toward the provincial capital Alexandria on 9 April 641. In late 641, Amr besieged Alexandria.

Amr ibn al-As.subject: Defence & Security
Amr ibn al-As.question: The date of the city's surrender was likely _____ 642
Amr ibn al-As.fact: The date of the city's surrender was likely November 642.

Amr ibn al-As.subject: Defence & Security
Amr ibn al-As.question: Taking advantage of the uncertain political situation in the wake of Umar's death in 644 and the meager Arab military presence in Alexandria, _____ II (r
Amr ibn al-As.fact: Taking advantage of the uncertain political situation in the wake of Umar's death in 644 and the meager Arab military presence in Alexandria, Emperor Constans II (r.

Amr ibn al-As.subject: Defence & Security
Amr ibn al-As.question: 641–668) dispatched a naval expedition led by a certain _____ which occupied the city and killed most of its Arab garrison in 645
Amr ibn al-As.fact: 641–668) dispatched a naval expedition led by a certain Manuel which occupied the city and killed most of its Arab garrison in 645. He besieged and captured Alexandria in the summer of 646; most of the Byzantines, including Manuel, were slain, many of its inhabitants were killed and the city was burned until Amr ordered an end to the onslaught.

Amr ibn al-As.subject: Defence & Security
Amr ibn al-As.question: Byzantine forces pushed deeper into the _____, but Amr forced them back at the Battle of Nikiou
Amr ibn al-As.fact: Byzantine forces pushed deeper into the Nile Delta, but Amr forced them back at the Battle of Nikiou.

Amr ibn al-As.subject: Defence & Security
Amr ibn al-As.question: Afterward, Muslim rule in _____ was gradually solidified
Amr ibn al-As.fact: Alexandria's elite and most of the inhabitants assisted the Byzantines; medieval Byzantine, Coptic and, to a lesser extent, Muslim sources indicate the city was not firmly in Arab hands during the preceding three years. He besieged and captured Alexandria in the summer of 646; most of the Byzantines, including Manuel, were slain, many of its inhabitants were killed and the city was burned until Amr ordered an end to the onslaught.

Amr ibn al-As.subject: Defence & Security
Amr ibn al-As.question: In the absence of siege engines, Amr oversaw long sieges of heavily fortified _____ positions, most prominently Babylon, cut supply lines and engaged in long wars of attrition
Amr ibn al-As.fact: In contrast to the disarray of the Byzantine defense, the Muslim forces under Amr's command were unified and organized; Amr frequently coordinated with Caliph Umar and his own troops for all major military decisions. According to the historian Vassilios Christides, Amr "cautiously counterbalanced the superiority in numbers and equipment of the Byzantine army by applying skillful military tactics" and despite the lack of "definite, prepared, long-term plans, the Arab army moved with great flex...

Amr ibn al-As.subject: Defence & Security
Amr ibn al-As.question: His cavalry-dominated army moved through _____'s deserts and oases with relative ease
Amr ibn al-As.fact: His cavalry-dominated army moved through Egypt's deserts and oases with relative ease.

Amr ibn al-As.subject: Defence & Security
Amr ibn al-As.question: Moreover, political circumstances became more favorable to Amr with the death of the hawkish _____ and his short-term replacement with the more pacifist Heraklonas and Martina.
Amr ibn al-As.fact: Moreover, political circumstances became more favorable to Amr with the death of the hawkish Heraclius and his short-term replacement with the more pacifist Heraklonas and Martina.

Amr ibn al-As.subject: Defence & Security
Amr ibn al-As.question: Toward the end of the year, Amr launched a second cavalry assault targeting _____

Assam Rifles.question: The AR is one of the _____-military Forces of India administered by the Ministry of Home Affairs while operational control rests with Indian Army
Assam Rifles.fact: The Assam Rifles (AR) is a paramilitary force of India responsible for border security, counter-insurgency, and maintaining law and order in Northeast India and in Jammu & Kashmir in lines of Rashtriya Rifles. Assam Rifles.question: In concert with the _____, they also undertook a number of expeditions into remote tribal areas along the north-east frontier and into Burma
Assam Rifles.fact: Elements of the force were also utilised in India during the war, being used to maintain internal security in order to free up troops from the army for use overseas.  During this time, the most notable action occurred in 1917 when columns of the Assam Rifles were despatched to Patna, to restore law and order in the riot-torn city.  After the war the force returned to northern India where they were used to maintain security amidst growing civil unrest and disorder.  In concert with the British Indian Army, they also undertook a number of expeditions into remote tribal areas along the north-east frontier and into Burma.  In 1924 they were sent to Malabar, which was then still part of the Madras Presidency, to carry out operations against the Mopla rebels.  === World War II === During World War II, the role of the Assam Rifles evolved once more as they were called upon to undertake even more varied tasks due to their status as both a police and military organisation. Assam Rifles.subject: Defence & Security
Assam Rifles.question: They also organized a resistance group on the Indo–_____ border to counter the Japanese invasion and to harass the enemy line of communications
Assam Rifles.fact: This time, however, their service would be undertaken closer to home.  After the lightning Japanese advance in 1942, the Assam Rifles fought a number of Independent actions behind enemy lines as the task of rear-area defence and rear-guard often fell to them during the Allies retreat into India.  Later, as a large influx of refugees fled from the advancing Japanese into India, the Assam Rifles were given the task of managing and organising this mass of humanity.  They also organized a resistance group on the Indo–Burmese border to counter the Japanese invasion and to harass the enemy line of communications.  This group became known as "Victor Force" (or sometimes V-Force), and the nucleus of it was formed from platoons made up of men from the Assam Rifles.  As part of this force, Assam Rifles platoons were used as covering forces during the latter stages of the Burma Campaign.  Other elements fought in the defensive "boxes" around Kohima, whilst another, from the 4th Battalion, trained as airborne troops, was dropped near the Sittang River behind Japanese lines

Border Security Force.question: This attack exposed the inadequacy of the _____ in coping with armed aggression
Border Security Force.fact: BSF has been termed the First Line of Defence of Indian territories.  == History == Since India's independence in 1947, the protection of its international boundaries was the responsibility of the local police in each border state, with little inter-state coordination.  However, during the Indo-Pakistani War of 1965, Pakistan attacked Sardar Post, Char Bet, and Beria Bet on 9 April 1965, in Kutch.  This attack exposed the inadequacy of the State Armed Police in coping with armed aggression.  Thus, after the war, the government created the Border Security Force as a unified central agency with the specific mandate of guarding India's international borders.  This act brought greater cohesion to border security.  K F Rustamji, from the Indian Police Service, was the first Director General of the BSF

In fact, for the BSF the war on the eastern front had started well before the war actually broke out in December 1971.  BSF had trained, supported and formed part of Mukti Bahini and had entered erstwhile East Pakistan before the actual hostilities broke out.  The BSF played a very important role in the Liberation of Bangladesh, which Indira Gandhi and Sheikh Mujibur Rehman had also acknowledged.  Rustamji, IPS, was appointed as the first Director General of Border Security Force from 22 July 1965, to 30 September 1972, and the current DG is Praveen Kumar, IPS, since 15 January 2026.  === Engagements === Indo-Pakistani War of 1971 Operation Blue Star Operation Black Thunder Insurgency in Punjab Insurgency in Jammu and Kashmir Operation Vijay – Kargil War 2001 Bangladeshi-Indian border skirmishes 2001–2002 Operation Parakram – India-Pakistan Standoff 2013 India-Pakistan Border skirmishes 2014–15 India–Pakistan border skirmishes 2016–2018 India–Pakistan border skirmishes 2019 India–Pakistan border skirmishes 2025 India–Pakistan standoff == Roles == During peacetime Border guarding and security.
